questions.q: How is the total figure for **credit sales** usually ascertained when converting single entry records into a double entry format?
options: By analyzing the debit side of the Cash Book
By preparing a Total Creditors Control Account
By preparing a Total Debtors Control Account
By creating an Opening Statement of Affairs
questions.explain: When records are incomplete, the missing figure for credit sales can be deduced by constructing a **Total Debtors (Sales Ledger) Control Account**. By plotting the opening debtors, closing debtors, cash received from customers, and discounts allowed, the balancing figure on the debit side reveals the total credit sales.

questions.q: The following information relates to the creditors of a business: Opening creditors ₦8,000; Cash paid to suppliers ₦40,000; Discounts received ₦2,000; Closing creditors ₦12,000. What is the value of **credit purchases** for the year?
questions.explain:
To find Credit Purchases, prepare a Total Creditors Control Account or use the equation:
$$\text{Credit Purchases} = \text{Cash Paid} + \text{Discounts Received} + \text{Closing Creditors} - \text{Opening Creditors}$$
$$\text{Credit Purchases} = ₦40,000 + ₦2,000 + ₦12,000 - ₦8,000$$
$$\text{Credit Purchases} = ₦54,000 - ₦8,000 = ₦46,000$$
